title: “The Morbs” is now playing Off-Broadway at A.R.T./New York through No...
transcript: It's Morbin time! I just saw the morbs. It is about three former sorority sisters who get cooped up in a cabin together as a mysterious illness known as the morbs rages on outside. And as the play goes on, we find out more about what the morbs is, how society has responded. We even meet someone who had the morbs but survived and has now become what's known as a hollow person, which is someone who has lost all attachment to their sense of self. And I don't wanna say too much more because a lot of the fun of this play is putting together the puzzle pieces that you get throughout. this play is constantly drip feeding you pieces of world building. And so as the play goes on, you're getting to see more and more of the picture. But at its core, this is a show about female friendship, as we see these three women who haven't seen each other in five years reconnect even though their lives have taken them in new directions and they're very much different people than they were in college. Yet I found myself not quite wanting to let myself invest in these relationships because I was constantly aware of this looming presence of the Morbs and this fear and paranoia of, like, who's gonna get it? Do they already have it? Just waiting for the other shoe to drop. And I realized that it was actually evoking a similar feeling that I Felt during the COVID 19 pandemic. this fear that COVID could be around the corner, that anyone at any time could give it to you, and the effect that that fear had on our lives and our relationships. The Morbs is obviously about a fictional pandemic, but it might also be the piece of media that I've seen that comes the closest to capturing what it's like to live through an actual real life pandemic, and I found it incredibly captivating. So the Morbs is going to be a strong Broadway Ben recommendation.
